title: Keychain files
whyItMatters: Keychains hold saved passwords, certificates and secure notes for websites, mail and networks. Their presence shows what the account could unlock.
source: SWGDE macOS tech notes 13-F-002-2.0 and mac forensics cheat sheet: macOS keychain files in ~/Library/Keychains
notes: Metadata only: file names, sizes and timestamps. Keychain databases are never opened, unlocked or parsed, and iCloud Keychain copies are out of scope.

cleanup.exportFirst: Save the passwords and secure notes you need with the export in the Passwords app or Keychain Access into a manager you keep.
cleanup.signOut: Turn iCloud Keychain off for this Mac in the iCloud settings under your Apple Account, so saved items stop syncing here.
steps: Turn iCloud Keychain off for this Mac in System Settings > Apple Account > iCloud first, so removing items here does not remove them from your other devices.
Open Keychain Access and delete the passwords and notes you saved yourself, one item at a time.
Do not delete the login keychain or the folder named in the plan by hand; macOS needs them, and the full reset clears them.
cleanup.risk: Saved website and app passwords, certificates and secure notes leave this Mac. Items kept only here cannot be recovered.
cleanup.source: Apple Support, Keychain Access User Guide: https://support.apple.com/guide/keychain-access/welcome/mac
